person.note: Seventh abbot of sNar thang monastery (ID:4411). On his dates see [2X2E3882]: 260, n. 146.

person.persName: bcom ldan rigs pa'i ral gri
person.note: On his career, see [KHA9ZVGP]: 3-8. The dates 1227-1305 are known from the biography (see work (ID:7016)) composed by his student bSam gtan bzang po (ID:4005) ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3). His name in religion was Dar ma rgyal mtshan or Chos kyi rgyal mtshan ([FZ6N88AU]: 406) - the name Chos kyi rgyal mtshan is given as his "real name" (mtshan dngos) in a homage by Rong ston ([KM47ZZDJ]: 657 and n. 62). The majority of the colophons of his works name him "bCom ldan ral gri," a few "Rigs/Rig pa’i ral gri" or just "Ral gri." Schwabland's discussion of the variants “Rigs pa” and “Rig pa” does not come to a definite conclusion as to which is the correct spelling ([CTQMVBPR]: 2-3). He was born as the son of a local wealthy headman, the fourth of five sons and his birth is reported to have been foretold by Śākyaśrībhadra (ID:6418) when he was invited by Ral gri's paternal uncle ([KHA9ZVGP]: 3).

bibl.title: chos bshad nyan la 'jug pa snang byed 'od zer rab tu rgyas pa
ཆོས་བཤད་ཉན་ལ་འཇུག་པ་སྣང་བྱེད་འོད་ཟེར་རབ་ཏུ་རྒྱས་པ
dbu ma tshig gsal gyi spyi don
bibl.author: skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims
bibl.note:
In spite of the title on the cover page of instance (ID:4832), is not a commentary of or introduction to the Prasannapadā (ID:3724). The incipit refers to a "general introduction to teaching the dharma" (chos bshad la 'jug pa spyi'i don). The text lists Madhyamaka treatises, gives biographies of Nāgārjuna (ID:3720) and Candrakīrti (ID:3725), etc. but does not actually engage with the Prasannapadā (ID:3724).
The author composed a dBu ma tshig gsal gyi bsdus don, see (ID:7588).

bibl.title: theg chen rgyud bla ma'i gdams pa
ཐེག་ཆེན་རྒྱུད་བླ་མའི་གདམས་པ
bibl.author: skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims
bibl.note:
Instruction on the Buddha nature, without direct citations of the Ratnagotravibhāga (ID:3749). Discussed in [FUFWUVQQ] and translated on pp. 310-318.
The text ends with the history of the transmission (lo rgyus) of the teaching of the Ratnagotravibhāga (ID:3749) along with the Dharmadharmatāvibhaṅga (ID:5634). The list, which does not include rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786), ends with Ze'u Chos kyi rgyal mtshan (ID:6458), preceded by sKyo ston (ID:4052) - considered to be the author of the present work. See [FUFWUVQQ]: 305 and 317-318 and [BAQ9MH4T]: 45-47.

bibl.title: bslabs btus dang spyod 'jug gi khrid
བསླབས་བཏུས་དང་སྤྱོད་འཇུག་གི་ཁྲིད

bibl.author: lha btsun pa
skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims
bibl.note: The manuscript (ID:5856) contains two parts, entitled respectively "bslab btus kyi bsgom don dpe'i khrid zab po" and "spyod 'jug 'khor lo lta bu'i lam mdor bsdus pa." They describe respectively shortly the contents of the chapters of the Śikṣāsamuccaya (ID:3742) and of the Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID:3727). There is a single transmission lineage for both works at the end in (ID:4840), the work reports a teaching transmitted in a lineage starting with Maitreya, down to sKyo ston (ID:4052), and written down in the course of its transmission to Chos kyi rgyal mtshan (ID:6458). However, the colophon of the second part names the author as "lha btsun pa," a scholar active at mChad kha dgon, who may be different from sKyo ston.

bibl.author: skyo ston smon lam tshul khrims
bibl.note: The colophon reports the author's name as "slob dpon pad mA" and the scribe's name as "ze'u." The author is sKyo ston (ID:4052) or Rigs pa'i ral gri (ID:4006). In the former case, the scribe is likely the same as for other works of sKyo ston, i.e., Ze'u Chos kyi rgyal mtshan (ID:6458). In the latter case, the scribe might rather be Ze'u Grags pa shes rab (ID:4065), scribe for two other works by Rigs pa'i ral gri. According to [CTSKHPIC]: 174, n. 167, this is not a work by Rigs pa'i ral gri. BDRC identifies the author as sKyo ston for bdr:MW1PD153536, and as Ze'u Grags pa shes rab (ID:4065) for bdr:WA0XL7E18A489111E (both entries are for the same manuscript, (ID:5096), printed twice in the [ZZVAXS4X]).
